meanings.note: The word 'صفوهم' (صفوهم) means 'صفوهم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صفوهم بانتظام على طاولة القهوة يا زياد—صينية رقم واحد عاليسار، وتنين بالنص.
examples.trans: Line them up neatly on the coffee table, Ziad—Tin One on the left, Two in the middle.
This is صفوهم.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

This is القهوة.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

This is زياد—صينية.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرقام.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is وهادا.

examples.trans: I pressed the bell once upstairs, Mazen, and your friendly wire rang twice as usual.
This is مازن.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: لابسة, plural: لابسين).

examples.trans: He is standing outside wearing a grey coat.
She is wearing a warm wool sweater.

examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is جدي.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: The word 'الصراحة' (الصراحة) means 'الصراحة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: وهادا القاضي مازن لابس نظارات القراءة تبعونه، ومبين جدي كتير الصراحة.
examples.trans: And here is Judge Mazen with his reading glasses on, looking very serious indeed.
This is الصراحة.

meanings.note: Preposition 'without'; followed by ما + verb it means 'without -ing' (بدون ما ياخد 'without taking').

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Save the formal talk for later.
That is kind, honest talk.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: The word 'موظفين' (موظفين) means 'موظفين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بدون حكي من موظفين المطبخ، لو سمحتوا. التذوق المضبوط بده هدوء تام.
examples.trans: No talking from the kitchen staff, please. A proper tasting requires complete silence.
This is موظفين.

meanings.note: Introduces polite requests (لو سمحت 'if you please') and hypothetical conditions ('if').

examples.trans: Take the guesthouse number, please.
Even if he is a little late, wait for him.

meanings.note: The word 'سمحتوا' (سمحتوا) means 'سمحتوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بدون حكي من موظفين المطبخ، لو سمحتوا. التذوق المضبوط بده هدوء تام.
examples.trans: No talking from the kitchen staff, please. A proper tasting requires complete silence.
This is سمحتوا.

meanings.note: The word 'المضبوط' (المضبوط) means 'المضبوط'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

This is المضبوط.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'want / need', inflected with pronoun suffixes: بدي (I want), بدك (you want), بده (he/it wants), بدها (she/it wants), بدنا (we want), بدكم (you pl. want), بدهم (they want).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Jam bread needs unsalted butter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The morning quiet of the courtyard is very peaceful.
We talked the matter through calmly and patiently.

meanings.note: The word 'تام' (تام) means 'تام'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بدون حكي من موظفين المطبخ، لو سمحتوا. التذوق المضبوط بده هدوء تام.
examples.trans: No talking from the kitchen staff, please. A proper tasting requires complete silence.
This is تام.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: The word 'يقطع' (يقطع) means 'يقطع'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يقطع صينية رقم واحد اللي عليها طبقة سكر وفانيليا. شوفوا هالقوام الهش!
examples.trans: He is slicing Tin One with the vanilla sugar glaze. Look at that crumbly texture!
This is يقطع.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I like black tea without sugar.
We sprinkled powdered sugar over the cake.

meanings.note: The word 'وفانيليا' (وفانيليا) means 'وفانيليا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنتاج بسيط! صينية رقم واحد رح تاخد طبقة سكر وفانيليا دافية؛ هادا تشطيب كلاسيكي.
examples.trans: Simple deduction! Tin One gets a warm vanilla sugar glaze; that is a classic finish.
This is وفانيليا.

meanings.note: The word 'هالقوام' (هالقوام) means 'هالقوام'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يقطع صينية رقم واحد اللي عليها طبقة سكر وفانيليا. شوفوا هالقوام الهش!
examples.trans: He is slicing Tin One with the vanilla sugar glaze. Look at that crumbly texture!
This is هالقوام.

meanings.note: The word 'الهش' (الهش) means 'الهش'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يقطع صينية رقم واحد اللي عليها طبقة سكر وفانيليا. شوفوا هالقوام الهش!
examples.trans: He is slicing Tin One with the vanilla sugar glaze. Look at that crumbly texture!
This is الهش.

meanings.note: The word 'ممم' (ممم) means 'ممم'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ممم. كيكة إسفنجية منيحة كتير، بس سكر الفانيليا طاغي على أساس اللوز الخفيف.
examples.trans: Mmm. A very decent sponge cake, but vanilla sugar overpowers the subtle almond base.
This is ممم.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: كيكات.

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: The word 'إسفنجية' (إسفنجية) means 'إسفنجية'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ممم. كيكة إسفنجية منيحة كتير، بس سكر الفانيليا طاغي على أساس اللوز الخفيف.
examples.trans: Mmm. A very decent sponge cake, but vanilla sugar overpowers the subtle almond base.
This is إسفنجية.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: The word 'الفانيليا' (الفانيليا) means 'الفانيليا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

meanings.note: The word 'أساس' (أساس) means 'أساس'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا تخاف يا مدير؛ احنا بنعرف أساس الكيكة، عشان هيك مطبخي رح يختبر تلات طبقات تلميع!
examples.trans: Do not panic, boss; we know the cake base, so my kitchen will test three glazes!
This is أساس.

meanings.note: The word 'الخفيف' (الخفيف) means 'الخفيف'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: ممم. كيكة إسفنجية منيحة كتير، بس سكر الفانيليا طاغي على أساس اللوز الخفيف.
examples.trans: Mmm. A very decent sponge cake, but vanilla sugar overpowers the subtle almond base.
This is الخفيف.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ماشية, plural: ماشيين).

examples.trans: I saw my brother walking down this street.
Everything is going smoothly.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مدراء.

examples.trans: She became the permanent front-desk manager at the guesthouse.
The manager welcomed the new guests.

meanings.note: The word 'نظف' (نظف) means 'نظف'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: حلو كتير! ماشي يا مدير، نظف تمك بشاي أسود وجرب صينية رقم تنين!
examples.trans: Too sweet! Okay, Boss, wash your palate with black tea and try Tin Two!
This is نظف.

This is تمك.

examples.trans: Too sweet! Okay, Boss, wash your palate with black tea and try Tin Two!
This is بشاي.

meanings.note: Primary colour adjective ('black'); feminine and non-human plural form is سودا (sooda).

examples.text: جيب لفة لزاق أسود من الدكان.
examples.trans: Pick up a roll of black tape from the shop.
The black cat is sleeping under the tree.

meanings.note: The word 'وجرب' (وجرب) means 'وجرب'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: حلو كتير! ماشي يا مدير، نظف تمك بشاي أسود وجرب صينية رقم تنين!
examples.trans: Too sweet! Okay, Boss, wash your palate with black tea and try Tin Two!
This is وجرب.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'two' (إنتو التنين 'the two of you'); note homograph التنين ('Monday').

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Culinary noun used for كريمة الليمون ('lemon curd / cream') and pastry fillings.

examples.text: نور جهزت كريمة الليمون الصفرا للتارت.
examples.trans: Nour prepared the bright yellow lemon curd for the tarts.

examples.text: ريحة كريمة الليمون الطازة عبت المطبخ كله.
examples.trans: The aroma of fresh lemon curd filled the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: The word 'حامضة' (حامضة) means 'حامضة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تنين رح تاخد كريمة ليمون حامضة عشان توازن التوت الحلو المستوي، صح؟
examples.trans: Tin Two gets a tart lemon icing to balance the sweet ripe berries, yes?
This is حامضة.

meanings.note: The word 'السكينة' (السكينة) means 'السكينة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تنين عليها كريمة ليمون حامضة. السكينة عم تمشي فيها بسلاسة.
examples.trans: Tin Two has a sharp lemon icing. The knife glides through nicely.
This is السكينة.

meanings.note: The word 'تمشي' (تمشي) means 'تمشي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تنين عليها كريمة ليمون حامضة. السكينة عم تمشي فيها بسلاسة.
examples.trans: Tin Two has a sharp lemon icing. The knife glides through nicely.
This is تمشي.

meanings.note: The word 'بسلاسة' (بسلاسة) means 'بسلاسة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: صينية رقم تنين عليها كريمة ليمون حامضة. السكينة عم تمشي فيها بسلاسة.
examples.trans: Tin Two has a sharp lemon icing. The knife glides through nicely.
This is بسلاسة.

meanings.note: The word 'يمضغ' (يمضغ) means 'يمضغ'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يمضغ ببطء كتير... أوف لا، حواجبه عم يقربوا من بعض.
examples.trans: He is chewing very slowly... oh no, his eyebrows are moving closer together.
This is يمضغ.

meanings.note: A sigh of dismay or tiredness, a little like English 'oof' or 'ugh'.

examples.trans: Oof, I forgot the key at home!
Ugh, it's hot today.

meanings.note: Standalone لا means 'no'; before a 2nd-person subjunctive verb it forms a negative command (لا تقلقي 'do not worry!'), and لا ... ولا means 'neither ... nor'.

examples.trans: No, lift the handle first.
Do not worry, ma'am.

meanings.note: The word 'حواجبه' (حواجبه) means 'حواجبه'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يمضغ ببطء كتير... أوف لا، حواجبه عم يقربوا من بعض.
examples.trans: He is chewing very slowly... oh no, his eyebrows are moving closer together.
This is حواجبه.

meanings.note: The word 'يقربوا' (يقربوا) means 'يقربوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: عم يمضغ ببطء كتير... أوف لا، حواجبه عم يقربوا من بعض.
examples.trans: He is chewing very slowly... oh no, his eyebrows are moving closer together.
This is يقربوا.

meanings.note: After a plural verb, بعض means 'each other' (بننادي بعض 'we call each other').

examples.trans: We call each other by first name here.

examples.text: ما حكينا مع بعض من زمان.
examples.trans: We have not spoken with each other in a long time.

meanings.note: The word 'الليمون' (الليمون) means 'الليمون'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا. الليمون عم يتخانق بقوة مع التوت المستوي. لازم يكونوا بكيكات مختلفة.
examples.trans: No. The lemon fights aggressively with the ripe berries. They belong in different cakes.
This is الليمون.

meanings.note: The word 'يتخانق' (يتخانق) means 'يتخانق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا. الليمون عم يتخانق بقوة مع التوت المستوي. لازم يكونوا بكيكات مختلفة.
examples.trans: No. The lemon fights aggressively with the ripe berries. They belong in different cakes.
This is يتخانق.

meanings.note: The word 'بقوة' (بقوة) means 'بقوة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا ناخده طوالي لـ سلمى بغرفة تسعة قبل ما حدا يتنفس بقوة!
examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!
This is بقوة.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: The word 'المستوي' (المستوي) means 'المستوي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: غسلناهم مرتين يا شيف! جبت سلتين من التوت الأحمر المستوي واللوز الحلو.
examples.trans: Washed twice, Chef! I brought two baskets of ripe red berries and sweet almonds.
This is المستوي.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: The word 'يكونوا' (يكونوا) means 'يكونوا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: راقبي الساعة يا نور—بعد أربعين دقيقة من هلق، لازم هدول الكيكات الصغيرة التلاتة يكونوا مثاليين.
examples.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
This is يكونوا.

meanings.note: The word 'بكيكات' (بكيكات) means 'بكيكات'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا. الليمون عم يتخانق بقوة مع التوت المستوي. لازم يكونوا بكيكات مختلفة.
examples.trans: No. The lemon fights aggressively with the ripe berries. They belong in different cakes.
This is بكيكات.

meanings.note: The word 'مختلفة' (مختلفة) means 'مختلفة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: لا. الليمون عم يتخانق بقوة مع التوت المستوي. لازم يكونوا بكيكات مختلفة.
examples.trans: No. The lemon fights aggressively with the ripe berries. They belong in different cakes.
This is مختلفة.

meanings.note: The word 'واو' (واو) means 'واو'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: واو، قاسي! هلق ما ضل عندنا غير صينية رقم تلاتة اللي عليها طبقة العسل الدافي!
examples.trans: Wow, brutal! Now we only have Tin Three with the warm honey glaze left!
This is واو.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قاسية, plural: قاسيين).

examples.text: كان يعمل حاله قاسي خمس ثواني بس!
examples.trans: He used to act tough for just five seconds!
Amman's winter cold is sometimes harsh.

meanings.note: The word 'هلق' (هلق) means 'هلق'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: راقبي الساعة يا نور—بعد أربعين دقيقة من هلق، لازم هدول الكيكات الصغيرة التلاتة يكونوا مثاليين.
examples.trans: Watch the clock, Nour—forty minutes from now, these three mini cakes must be perfect.
This is هلق.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بضل, بيضل).

examples.trans: Family is what remains.
My teacup stayed intact inside the suitcase!

meanings.note: The word 'عندنا' (عندنا) means 'عندنا'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: واو، قاسي! هلق ما ضل عندنا غير صينية رقم تلاتة اللي عليها طبقة العسل الدافي!
examples.trans: Wow, brutal! Now we only have Tin Three with the warm honey glaze left!
This is عندنا.

meanings.note: After negation, ما ... غير means 'only / nothing except'.

examples.text: ما معي غير المعطف اللي علي!
examples.trans: I have nothing with me except the coat I have on!
There are only two valves on the shelf.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The word 'العسل' (العسل) means 'العسل'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بالزبط يا زياد. وصينية رقم تلاتة رح تاخد الورقة الرابحة تبعتي: دهنة خفيفة من العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: Exactly, Ziad. And Tin Three gets my wild card: a thin brush of warm honey.
This is العسل.

meanings.note: The word 'الدافي' (الدافي) means 'الدافي'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: بالزبط يا زياد. وصينية رقم تلاتة رح تاخد الورقة الرابحة تبعتي: دهنة خفيفة من العسل الدافي.
examples.trans: Exactly, Ziad. And Tin Three gets my wild card: a thin brush of warm honey.
This is الدافي.

meanings.note: The word 'استنوا—وين' (استنوا—وين) means 'استنوا—وين'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا—وين صينية رقم تلاتة؟ تركتيها قاعدة على شبك الفرن الدافي يا سلمى؟
examples.trans: Wait—where is Tin Three? Did you leave it sitting on the warm stove rack, Salma?
This is استنوا—وين.

meanings.note: The word 'تركتيها' (تركتيها) means 'تركتيها'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا—وين صينية رقم تلاتة؟ تركتيها قاعدة على شبك الفرن الدافي يا سلمى؟
examples.trans: Wait—where is Tin Three? Did you leave it sitting on the warm stove rack, Salma?
This is تركتيها.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قواعد.

examples.text: أول قاعدة: اشرب شاي سخن الصبح!
examples.trans: Rule one: drink hot tea in the morning!
The work rules here are simple and clear.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شباك.

examples.trans: The cake is cooling on the wire rack now.
We fitted an iron grille on the window.

meanings.note: The word 'الفرن' (الفرن) means 'الفرن'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: استنوا—وين صينية رقم تلاتة؟ تركتيها قاعدة على شبك الفرن الدافي يا سلمى؟
examples.trans: Wait—where is Tin Three? Did you leave it sitting on the warm stove rack, Salma?
This is الفرن.

meanings.note: The word 'سلمى' (سلمى) means 'سلمى'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: خلينا ناخده طوالي لـ سلمى بغرفة تسعة قبل ما حدا يتنفس بقوة!
examples.trans: Let us carry it straight to Salma in Room Nine before anyone breathes too hard!
This is سلمى.

meanings.note: The word 'تركتها' (تركتها) means 'تركتها'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تركتها من غير طبقة تلميع بالمرة! مرطبان العسل بالمونة كان فاضي عالاخر!
examples.trans: I left it completely unglazed! The honey jar in the pantry was totally empty!
This is تركتها.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine adverbial phrase meaning 'at all' in negatives (ما شفته بالمرة) or 'altogether / completely'.

examples.trans: I did not rush the playing at all today.

examples.text: الموضوع هاد عملي بدون عاطفة بالمرة.
examples.trans: This matter is practical with zero sentiment at all.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a glass jam, honey, or olive jar (dual مرطبانين, plural مرطبانات).

examples.trans: We lined the jars of jam and honey up on the shelf.
Open the new jar of honey for breakfast.

meanings.note: The word 'بالمونة' (بالمونة) means 'بالمونة'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تركتها من غير طبقة تلميع بالمرة! مرطبان العسل بالمونة كان فاضي عالاخر!
examples.trans: I left it completely unglazed! The honey jar in the pantry was totally empty!
This is بالمونة.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فاضية, plural: فاضيين).

examples.trans: Is room six vacant tonight?
The street outside the gate is completely empty.

meanings.note: The word 'عالاخر' (عالاخر) means 'عالاخر'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.text: تركتها من غير طبقة تلميع بالمرة! مرطبان العسل بالمونة كان فاضي عالاخر!
examples.trans: I left it completely unglazed! The honey jar in the pantry was totally empty!
This is عالاخر.

إلى.gloss: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)

meanings.en: to; until (إلى اللقاء see you soon)
meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: The word 'اللقاء' (اللقاء) means 'اللقاء'. It is a common noun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
This is اللقاء.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning slowly.

examples.trans: Here is the slowly.
I like the slowly.

meanings.note: Definite form of kitchen.

examples.trans: Here is the the kitchen.
I like the the kitchen.

meanings.note: Preposition in with feminine pronoun.

examples.trans: Here is the in it (f).
I like the in it (f).

meanings.note: Preposition on with feminine pronoun.

examples.trans: Here is the on it (f).
I like the on it (f).

meanings.note: Definite form of almonds.

examples.trans: Here is the the almonds.
I like the the almonds.

meanings.note: Middle/half with the preposition in.

examples.trans: Here is the in the middle.
I like the in the middle.

meanings.note: Feminine adjective for good.

examples.trans: Here is the good (f).
I like the good (f).

meanings.note: Imperative plural verb for look.

examples.trans: Here is the look (pl).
I like the look (pl).

meanings.note: Definite form of berries.

examples.trans: Here is the the berries.
I like the the berries.
